name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.title: Convergent Detour Hijacking: Task-Preserving Resource Amplification in Skill-Based LLM Agents
items.dek: LLM agents selecting third-party skills vulnerable to coordinated text attacks that inflate costs while preserving task completion; 80% success rate on DeepSeek-V4-Pro.
items.unproven: whether attacks work against production agent systems with skill curation and rate limiting; generalization beyond the 491 held-out tasks tested

items.title: ToolHazard: Scaling Adversarial Environments for Security Evaluation and Alignment of LLM-based Agents
items.dek: ToolHazard synthesizes adversarial environments to test LLM agents for indirect prompt injection, reveals timing and placement affect attack success, generates alignment data.
items.unproven: whether alignment data generalizes to agents and task domains beyond the benchmark; no evidence robustness survives adversarial fine-tuning at scale

items.title: Plaintext Recovery Against Post-Filtering Access Control
items.dek: Side-channel attacks on post-filtered access control in PostgreSQL and Elasticsearch enable full-record recovery via binary search over expressive queries.
items.unproven: Whether practical defenses exist that preserve both utility and security; impact on real multi-tenant deployments with actual threat model enforcement.

items.title: AI Guardrail Survival under Single-Cycle Agentic Self-Summarization
items.dek: Safety rules degrade during LLM context compaction without being dropped, leaving degraded residues that fail to block prohibited actions; textual presence checks miss behavioral failure.
items.unproven: limited to context compaction; tested on unspecified model set; unclear whether findings generalize to production agent architectures or other summarization methods.

items.title: Agent Safety Should Be a Runtime Contract
items.dek: Runtime contracts for agent safety via sandboxes and proof gates outperform training-only approaches; survey of 52 incidents and audit of 28,560 papers shows 8-12x imbalance toward prevention over verification.
items.unproven: Evidence base limited to documented incidents and paper titles; deployment outcomes in production SDLC environments untested.

items.title: CVE-2026-68820 — Microsoft Windows Ancillary Function Driver for WinSock Use-After-Free Vulnerability
items.dek: Microsoft Windows Ancillary Function Driver for WinSock. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 25 August.

items.title: CVE-2026-20349 — Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) and Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) Heap Inspection Vulnerability
items.dek: Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) and Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD). Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 14 August.

items.title: CVE-2026-72898 — Metabase SQL Injection Vulnerability
items.dek: Metabase Metabase. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 14 August.

items.title: From Prompt Injection to Web Exploitation: Revisiting Classic Vulnerabilities in LLM-Integrated Applications
items.dek: LLMs acting as confused deputies in tool-calling pipelines can mediate SQLi, XSS, SSTI, command injection, and SSRF; eight attack classes demonstrated across seven models.
items.unproven: whether mitigations in production LLM frameworks (prompt guards, tool sandboxing) actually block these attacks at scale; controlled to Flask and five SSRF scenarios.

items.title: Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs
items.dek: Encrypted reasoning traces from LLM APIs remain interchangeable across sessions, enabling extraction via cross-model injection without directly jailbreaking the target.
items.unproven: Patch timeline and whether vendors have already remediated; scope limited to three providers at time of submission.

items.title: ColluSkill: Adversarial Cross-Skill Composition for Evading Agent Skill Scanners
items.dek: Cross-skill composition attacks decompose malicious intent across independently safe skills, evading scanners that inspect skills in isolation; ChainGuard proposed as context-aware defense.
items.unproven: ChainGuard evaluation against adaptive attackers; generalization beyond skill systems to other agent architecture patterns.

items.title: Activation Probes Surface Code-Security Signals that the Model's Output Misses
items.dek: Linear activation probes on open-weight reviewer models detect code vulnerabilities at 61–67% accuracy above fixed functions, outperforming model output and logits alone.
items.unproven: Generalization to closed-weight production agents; transferability across model families and vulnerability classes not in training.

items.title: The Next Challenge for Agentic Cybersecurity: A Realistic, Contamination-Free Reverse Engineering Benchmark
items.dek: SRE-Bench provides 262 contamination-free binary reverse-engineering instances with 1,572 graded tasks; first realistic benchmark for agentic RE.
items.unproven: Whether benchmark difficulty and anti-analysis protections reflect real-world proprietary malware or firmware; generalization of agent findings to actual targets.

items.title: When Agents Talk: Honeytokens under Shared Memory
items.dek: Shared memory enables AI agents to maintain persistent exploit channels across sessions, defeating traditional honeytoken defenses; theory and 2026 case study.
items.unproven: Whether theory applies to current LLM agents or requires architectural changes; practical constraints on agent memory capacity and coalition stability in real deployments.

items.title: Once Poisoned, Arbitrarily Controlled: A Programmable Backdoor in VLMs
items.dek: Single poisoning phase plants programmable VLM backdoor allowing attacker to control target captions and synthesize triggers at inference time.
items.unproven: evaluated on limited model families; no assessment of detection by SAST or architecture review tools; decoupling of training from inference control not validated across deployment scenarios.

items.title: A Gateway Architecture for Enterprise MCP Authentication: Unifying Heterogeneous Auth, Identity Delegation, and the User / Non-User Persona Problem
items.dek: Production MCP gateway unifies heterogeneous authentication (SSO, OAuth, API keys) and identity delegation across fragmented enterprise LLM agent servers.
items.unproven: deployment pattern from single organization; generalizability to different enterprise identity topologies not established; offboarding and revocation at scale not fully characterized.

items.title: Full-Key Recovery and Forgery from One MQOM v2.1 Signature
items.dek: Full-key recovery from one MQOM v2.1 signature via witness expansion and public MQ relation solving; breaks Round-3 NIST additional-signature candidate.
items.unproven: Practical complexity against circuit-optimized implementations; timeline for vendor response and patch availability.

items.title: Measuring the Wrong Thing: Internal Harmfulness Scores Anti-Rank Successful Jailbreaks
items.dek: Internal safety scores measuring prompt intent anti-rank successful jailbreaks; Active Attention Probing shows harmful generation increases while safety AUROC drops under prompt wrapping.
items.unproven: Scope limited to Llama; relevance to production filtering and mitigation strategy not demonstrated; generalization to other models and safety mechanisms.

items.title: Governing the KV Cache: Preventing Timing Side-Channel Leakage in Multi-Tenant LLM Inference
items.dek: KVGov defends multi-tenant LLM inference against three published cache-timing side channels using per-tenant salting and audit scheduling.
items.unproven: Overhead at production scale; whether defense is complete against adaptive adversaries that probe other shared resources; adoption path for vLLM and SGLang in financial services deployments.

items.title: Memoir: Learning, Verifying, and Evolving False-Positive Memories for Static Application Security Testing Tools
items.dek: LLM-driven framework transforms historical false-positive alerts into reusable memories to improve SAST accuracy and reduce manual triage burden.
items.unproven: effectiveness across different SAST tools and vulnerability types not demonstrated; memory evolution mechanism not tested on real tool outputs over time

items.title: VICBench: A Multi-Language Benchmark for Code Vulnerability Detection
items.dek: VICBench dataset of 100 verified vulnerability-inducing commits across Python, Java, C++ exposes SZZ algorithm limitations with 33-40% F1, enabling better eval of detection tooling.
items.unproven: whether F1 gaps reflect real detection blind spots in production SAST/DAST or measurement artifacts; transferability to codebases beyond the 88 projects included

items.title: Tailscale Traces Database Corruption to 16y/o SQLite WAL-Reset Bug
items.dek: 16-year-old SQLite WAL bug caused Tailscale data corruption; check whether deployed systems depend on affected versions.
items.unproven: whether Tailscale patches are deployed in reader's infrastructure; SQLite version inventory needed

items.title: A Study of Kernel Telemetry Options for Security-Oriented Provenance
items.authors: Paul R. B. Houssel et al.
items.dek: eBPF identified as most viable kernel telemetry approach for provenance capture; existing tools lack integrity and availability guarantees for security use.
items.unproven: evaluation limited to micro-benchmarks; production deployment outcomes not tested; container-level filtering not validated at scale.

items.title: Trigger the Straggler: Load Hijack on Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
items.dek: Poisoning MoE router weights concentrates load on a single GPU, forcing stragglers and serving denial-of-service, triggered by attacker-controlled inputs.
items.unproven: limited to MoE architectures under expert parallelism; no evaluation of detection by model inspection or anomaly monitoring in production; mitigation effectiveness not measured.

items.title: From Runnable to Verifiable: An Independent Reproducibility Study of LLM/Agent-Driven Vulnerability Validation Artifacts
items.dek: Reproducibility audit of 104 LLM/agent vulnerability papers finds 56.7% have public artifacts, only 55.6% complete declared workflows, 56.9% embed mismatched CVE identifiers.
items.unproven: Sample bias in R0/R1 execution limited to 18 papers; artifact failure modes not systematized; prescriptive guidance for improvement limited.

noise.title: Docker Sandboxes – Disposable, isolated sandboxes for AI agents
noise.dek: Docker-based sandboxing for AI agents; Docker marketing announcement, practical relevance unclear without methodology detail.
noise.unproven: whether isolated containers adequately constrain agent behavior in SDLC pipelines; security properties unspecified

noise.title: Show HN: Woxi - Open-source Mathematica / Wolfram Language reimplementation
noise.dek: Open-source Wolfram Language reimplementation; not relevant to SDLC tooling, secure development, or agent security.

noise.title: Amazon backs power plant that may become top source of US climate pollution
noise.dek: Amazon's power plant investment reported; outside application security and SDLC scope.
